Consult Summary:
- Evaluation for chronic dry, cracked palmar dermatitis likely related to occupational exposure; plan includes protective gloves and topical therapy with follow-up.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Soreness and cracking of skin on hands, mainly the palms; dry skin and itching; symptoms started about 3–4 months ago; worsened to interfere with work.
- Onset/progression: Gradual onset a few months ago; progression to painful cracking; intermittent itch; occasional bleeding with scratching.
- Associated symptoms: Itching; no fever, nausea, vomiting, bowel or urinary symptoms; appetite preserved.
- Past medical history: Diabetes mellitus type 2; on metformin (dose/frequency not documented).
- Medications: Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: None reported.
- Social history: Works as a hotel housekeeper; gloves not consistently worn; recently changed jobs (~4 months ago); non-smoker; drinks a small amount of alcohol (a couple of pints per week).
- Relevant exposures: Cleaning products; potential irritation from gloves/chemicals; potential correlation between exposure and skin symptoms.

Examination:
- (Not described in transcript.)

Impression:
- Dermatitis or contact dermatitis of the palms, likely related to occupational exposure to cleaning products and glove use.

Plan:
- Avoid triggers: wear gloves at all times when cleaning.
- Treatments: topical corticosteroid cream for inflammation (dose/route/frequency not documented); intensified emollient applied 3–4 times daily for the next 2 weeks.
- Follow-up: If no improvement after 1–2 weeks, or if symptoms spread or worsen, return sooner for re-evaluation.
- Medications: Prescription to pharmacy (specific steroid name not documented in transcript).
